transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Taking care of my mom on top of work has thrown my whole life off, and I feel like I’m not handling any of it the way I usually would. Ever since her stroke, everything has been completely upended, and I'm just feeling incredibly overwhelmed trying to manage it all.

Can you tell me more about what you mean by 'not handling things the way you usually would'? Are you experiencing any persistent feelings of sadness, hopelessness, or anxiety that are affecting your daily life?

I'm snapping at the guys at the shop over nothing and crying in the bathroom between oil changes, which is completely unlike me. It's gotten so bad that I had a near-miss safety incident at work, got warned by my supervisor, and have completely stopped going to church or my truck club. At night, I just lie awake blaming myself for dropping the ball on everything because I'm so exhausted and overwhelmed.
Have you been experiencing any recurring, distressing memories or flashbacks related to your mom's stroke or other traumatic events that are contributing to your feelings of overwhelm and self-blame?

No, I haven't been having any flashbacks or scary memories about the stroke itself. The overwhelm and self-blame are really just about the daily, ongoing struggle of trying to juggle her care with my job, rather than re-living that specific day.

Can you estimate how long you've been feeling this overwhelmed and struggling to manage your responsibilities, and has it been a constant feeling since your mom's stroke or have the feelings intensified over time?

It’s been going on for about four months now, starting within just a couple of weeks of my mom's stroke when I first began juggling her care and my job. It has definitely intensified over time, as the weeks of constant stress, mounting bills, and zero personal time have completely worn me down and made me much more reactive.

You mentioned stopping going to church and your truck club, which you used to enjoy; do you feel like you've lost interest in these activities or is it more that you just don't have the time or energy for them anymore?

I haven't lost interest at all; those activities used to keep me grounded and I really miss them. But right now, I'm just running on fumes trying to juggle work and my mom's care. There is absolutely no time or mental energy left for anything extra.
Even when you do get a brief moment to yourself or think about doing something you used to enjoy, do you still find pleasure in those activities, or has the pleasure been significantly diminished?

Honestly, any thought of those activities just brings on guilt and stress about dropping the ball rather than any real pleasure. I'm so exhausted and running on fumes that even thinking about going makes me feel overwhelmed. I really miss how they kept me grounded, but right now, there's just no room for enjoyment.

When you do manage to engage in one of these activities you used to enjoy, like briefly attending church or working on your truck, do you feel any sense of pleasure or satisfaction during that time, or is it completely absent?

To be honest, I haven't actually managed to engage in those activities at all lately. I've completely dropped out of church and the truck club because I'm just too exhausted and overwhelmed. I haven't even had the chance to try enjoying them because my time and energy are completely gone.
When you think back to the times before your mom's stroke, did you generally enjoy your daily activities and find pleasure in the things you did, or was it more of a neutral experience for you?

Oh, I absolutely loved my life and activities before all of this happened. My structured routine at the shop, going to church, and participating in my truck club and classic-truck events were things I truly enjoyed and that kept me grounded. It definitely wasn't a neutral experience—I was genuinely happy and looked forward to them.

You mentioned that thinking about your old activities brings guilt and stress, but when you reflect on your past enjoyment of them, it sounds like you genuinely found pleasure in those things; do you think if you had the time and energy, you would still be able to enjoy and find satisfaction in those activities, or do you feel like something fundamental has changed in how you experience pleasure?

I definitely think I would still enjoy them; my capacity for pleasure hasn't changed, I'm just completely exhausted and overwhelmed by everything right now. I really hope and expect that once my mom's situation stabilizes and I have some breathing room, I'll be able to get back to my normal routine and enjoy church and the truck club just like before.

Do you think that even if your external circumstances improved and you had more time and energy, you would still feel a lack of pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy, or would you expect your enjoyment of them to return?

Yes, I definitely expect my enjoyment of church and the truck club to return once my mom's health stabilizes and she doesn't need this intense level of care. I really believe that if the circumstances improved, I'd be able to get back to my normal routine and stop feeling so overwhelmed and strung out all the time.

You've mentioned that you expect to enjoy your activities again once your circumstances improve, but can you think of any activities, no matter how small, that you still find some pleasure in or look forward to, even if it's just slightly, during this difficult time?

Honestly, I can't really think of anything I enjoy or look forward to right now. I am just too overwhelmed by my caregiving duties and work responsibilities to find pleasure in anything. I've had to let go of all my usual hobbies, like church and the truck club, so there's really nothing left but stress and exhaustion.

Are there any activities or things that you still look forward to or find some small joy in, even if it's something as simple as a favorite meal, a warm bath, or a good book, despite feeling overwhelmed with your current responsibilities?

I used to find so much joy and grounding in my church activities and truck club meets, but I've completely dropped out of them lately. Right now, I'm just running on fumes and feel far too overwhelmed to enjoy or look forward to anything. I simply don't have the time or mental energy left for even small pleasures.

You've mentioned that you can't think of anything you enjoy or look forward to right now, but can you think of any times, even briefly, where you felt a slight sense of relief or comfort, such as a good conversation, a beautiful sunset, or a favorite meal, that might indicate some preservation of pleasure despite your current struggles?

I appreciate you asking, but I honestly can't think of any moments of relief or comfort lately. I am just so completely overwhelmed and exhausted by my current situation that I don't even register things like that anymore. My mind is constantly racing with everything I have to do, so there's just no room for those feelings right now.
Are there any small, everyday things that you still find slightly enjoyable, such as laughing with someone, reading, or spending time in nature, even if it's not as enjoyable as it used to be?
I honestly can't think of anything right now. I am just too exhausted and overwhelmed with my daily routine of work and caregiving to find enjoyment in much of anything.

Can you tell me if you've been experiencing excessive worry or fear about the future, such as worrying about your mom's health or your ability to care for her, that's contributing to your feelings of overwhelm?

Yes, I'm constantly terrified about the future, especially when it comes to managing my mom's daily medications and handling all of her mounting bills. I constantly worry about whether I can keep up with both my job and her care without failing at both, which distracts me at work and leaves me feeling like I'm running on fumes and dropping the ball.

Do you feel like your excessive worry and fear about the future, such as your mom's health and your ability to care for her, are more prominent and distressing to you than your feelings of sadness and loss of pleasure in activities?

I don't really think of it in those terms. Rather than having excessive worry about the future, I just feel completely overwhelmed, exhausted, and really sad and guilty about dropping the ball in my daily life right now.
Do you think your feelings of sadness, guilt, and loss of pleasure in activities are more distressing to you than your feelings of anxiety and worry about the future, or are they equally bothersome?
It's really hard to separate the two because they both feel incredibly overwhelming right now. I'm just so exhausted and stretched thin that I honestly aren't sure which one is actually worse.

When you're feeling overwhelmed, is it more the thoughts and worries about your responsibilities and your mom's care that are bothering you, or is it more the feelings of sadness, emptiness, and loss of interest in activities that you used to enjoy?

It’s really a mix of both. The constant worry about dropping the ball with my mom's care and my job is exhausting and keeps me up at night, but at the same time, I feel a deep sadness and have completely stopped going to church and the truck club because I'm just too drained to face them.

Can you tell me if there are any specific situations or triggers that make your feelings of anxiety and worry worse, or if they are more constant and related to your overall situation of caring for your mom and managing work?

It’s really a mix of both, because there is this constant, heavy baseline of worry about managing everything since my mom's stroke. But specific situations definitely spike it, like trying to coordinate her hospital visits during my work shifts, dealing with all the overwhelming financial paperwork and home modifications, or worrying about her medications while I'm at the shop—which actually led to a scary near-miss recently.

Do you think that if your anxiety and worries about your mom's care and your responsibilities were significantly reduced, you would still feel sad, empty, and uninterested in activities, or would those feelings also improve?

Yes, I definitely believe those feelings would improve. If my mom's health stabilized and she didn't need this constant level of care, I expect I'd be able to get back to my normal routine. I don't think I would feel so strung out and overwhelmed all the time if things went back to normal.

Do you think that your feelings of sadness and loss of interest in activities are a direct result of your overwhelming situation and anxiety about your mom's care, or do you feel like there's something more to your sadness that isn't just about your current stressors?

Yes, my sadness and pulling away from everything are completely because of the overwhelming pressure of juggling work and taking care of my mom. Before her stroke, I was doing completely fine and loved my life. I really believe that once her health stabilizes and she doesn't need this level of care, I'll be able to get back to my normal routine and feel like myself again.

Do you think that if your situation with your mom's care and work responsibilities improved significantly, your feelings of anxiety and worry would decrease more quickly than your feelings of sadness and loss of interest in activities?

I'm really not sure which of those feelings would fade first. I just hope that once things get easier and my mom's situation stabilizes, all of these heavy feelings will finally lift so I can get back to my normal life.

If your mom's health were to suddenly improve and you no longer had to care for her, do you think you would quickly return to your normal self and enjoy activities again, or would you expect it to take some time to adjust and feel better?

I truly believe that if my mom's health stabilized or she didn't need this intense level of care anymore, I'd be able to get back to my normal routine pretty quickly. I have a lot of hope that once that pressure is off, I'd stop feeling so constantly strung out and overwhelmed. I really think I'd be able to feel like myself again without too much trouble.

Do you think that your feelings of anxiety and worry about your mom's care and your responsibilities are the main drivers of your current distress, or are your feelings of sadness and loss of pleasure in activities equally or more bothersome to you?

They are deeply connected and feel equally heavy to me. The constant pressure of juggling my mom's care and my job drives my daily stress and makes me feel like I'm always dropping balls, but losing my outlets like church and the truck club and crying in the bathroom makes it feel like I have no escape, which is just as painful.

When you imagine your mom's health improving and your caregiving responsibilities easing, do you think your anxiety about the future would decrease first, followed by an improvement in your mood and interest in activities, or would you expect your mood and interest in activities to improve first, followed by a decrease in anxiety?

To be honest, I'm really not sure which of those would happen first. I just know that if my mom's health stabilized and things eased up, I'd expect to feel a lot less strung out and hopefully get back to my normal routine eventually.

If your mom's health suddenly improved and you were no longer responsible for her care, do you think you would quickly regain your interest in activities like church and the truck club, or would you need some time to adjust before enjoying them again?

I fully expect that if my mom's health stabilized and she didn't require this level of care anymore, I'd be able to get right back to my normal routine. I think I would quickly start enjoying church and the truck club again and stop feeling so constantly strung out. Getting that pressure off my shoulders would make all the difference.

Do you think that if your anxiety and worries about your mom's care and your responsibilities were completely gone, you would still feel a significant lack of pleasure in activities and a depressed mood, or would those feelings largely disappear along with the anxiety?

I really believe those feelings would largely disappear once the pressure was off. I keep telling myself that if my mom's situation stabilizes or she doesn't need this level of care anymore, I'll be able to get back to my normal routine and stop feeling so strung out and down all the time.

Do you think that your anxiety and worry about your mom's care and your responsibilities are the primary cause of your current feelings of sadness and loss of interest in activities, or do you feel like there's a deeper issue with your mood that's separate from your anxiety?

It's definitely all tied directly to the overwhelming stress of caring for my mom and balancing my job. I don't think there's a deeper, separate mood issue going on with me. I truly believe that if my mom's health stabilized and this heavy caregiving load was lifted, I'd be able to get right back to my normal, grounded self.
Do you think that your feelings of anxiety and worry are more of a problem for you right now, or are your feelings of sadness and lack of interest in activities the bigger issue?

It really feels like a mix of both. The sadness and lack of interest are huge because I've completely stopped going to church and my truck club, and I find myself crying in the bathroom at work. At the same time, the constant worry and stress keep me awake at night beating myself up and distract me at work as I worry about my mom's medications.

If you were to rate your current level of distress, would you say that your feelings of anxiety and worry about your mom's care and your responsibilities are more distressing to you, or your feelings of sadness, guilt, and loss of pleasure in activities?

It's really hard to separate the two because they feel completely intertwined right now. Both the constant worry about my mom's care and the deep sadness and guilt over losing my normal life and hobbies feel equally overwhelming. I honestly couldn't say one is worse than the other.
